changelog.title: Version Two
highlights: GOOD FIRST PICK now shows for everyone, every run, until you carry two weapons. Veterans who like a Coffee-only start can still pass on it.

changelog.title: Version Two
changelog.teaser: New hires get one piece of advice: bring more than coffee.
highlights: While Coffee is your only weapon, one level-up card is always a weapon that deals damage, marked GOOD FIRST PICK. The other two cards are the usual shuffle, and the choice is still yours.

changelog.title: Version Two
changelog.teaser: Stand still long enough and your hero gets on with their day.
highlights: New idle animations for all four heroes: Soccer Dad sips his coffee, the 9-to-5er pushes up his glasses, the Grad Student checks her notebook, and the Cold War Cowboy checks his floppy disk.
Standing still, your hero breathes. Every few seconds they blink and do their thing.

changelog.title: Version Two
changelog.teaser: The 30-Year Mortgage no longer takes the scenic route.
highlights: Maple Hollow bosses come out of their own part of town. They used to take up to two minutes to walk to you while the swarm piled up. Now they hurry while they're far away and slow down for the fight.

changelog.title: Version Two
changelog.teaser: You can finally see the whole neighborhood. It's mostly woods you're not allowed in yet.
highlights: Maple Hollow has a map. It's in the corner from the start (you know your own neighborhood). Tap it or press M for the whole town.
Areas that haven't opened show the age they open at. A newly opened area gets an orange outline until you visit.
Inside the house, the corner map shows the house.

changelog.title: Version Two
changelog.teaser: Something just opened. Everyone in town wants you to go look.
highlights: When a new part of Maple Hollow opens, a big wave of easy enemies (plus a couple of tough ones) rolls in from the other side and herds you toward it.
Arrows at the edge of the screen point to bosses and to newly opened areas, until you get there.
TJ and Derek now show up in Maple Hollow too, with their bonuses.

changelog.title: Version Two
changelog.teaser: New roads, real crosswalks, and a forest that is mostly trees now.
highlights: Every street in Maple Hollow is repainted, with crosswalks and T-junctions where the roads meet, chalk drawings, lost mittens and puddles.
Cars park along the north-south roads. They leave you a full lane, but don't count on them moving.
The woods around the closed areas are a real forest now: birch, maple and evergreen trees, a fallen log, mossy rocks and a mushroom ring. Two old standing stones wait outside Town Square.

changelog.title: Version Two
changelog.teaser: The kitchen has an island now. The TV is gone. Nobody knows where.
highlights: A kitchen island with stools, a bigger console in the dining room, and Abe's record dresser, cube shelf, hamper, amp and rug at their real sizes.
The living room TV is gone for now. The sim rig faces the wall and pretends.

memos.title: Achievement Unlocked: Gaussian Splatting.
memos.teaser: 212 photos of Abdel, a 3D scene I can fly a camera through, and a prompt so you can try it.

memos.title: Music is one of the most important side characters.
memos.teaser: Driving Abe to school, the songs that are the game, and an ask for help with its music.

memos.title: Restless. Also, who's actually playing?
memos.teaser: A stranger on Facebook, Paul, Kevin, and the game's first soundtrack.

memos.title: If that's where community is, that's where I want to be.
memos.teaser: The game got its own Discord, and it posts its own updates.

memos.title: This is starting to feel real.
memos.teaser: Version two, built on paternity leave, one feeding at a time.

memos.title: My friends work here now.
memos.teaser: TJ found a bug, Derek and TJ became interns with their own Lounge, Ben became the Coldwar Cowboy, and the game and the devlog finally feel like one thing.

memos.title: I got promoted four times before lunch.
memos.teaser: Promotions open six new rooms, almost everything breaks, bosses fight back, a sneaky bug made enemies run away, every weapon got a job, and the whole office moves smoother.

memos.title: My office got jokes. Then my enemies got smarter.
memos.teaser: Corporate slang became furniture, the swarm learned to walk around desks, dodging got a streak meter, and real playtesters told me what was broken.

memos.title: The office got bigger. Somebody lost a binder.
memos.teaser: The art preview grows an atrium, side wings and a records annex with a lost binder. The map fills in as you walk.

memos.title: There's a coffee button now. It feels weird.
memos.teaser: Asking for money feels weird, so here is exactly where it goes: more AI time to finish this game. Also, I am looking for people who want to help build it.

memos.title: I could beat my own game standing still. So I hired a robot.
memos.teaser: Four minutes in, I could put the controller down. A test bot, a Grok review and a Comfort Zone Tax fixed that.

memos.title: The office has seen a few restructurings.
memos.teaser: Accounts Payable gets desks with personality, a jammed printer, and a plant that needs PTO.

memos.title: The office has people in it now. And they walk.
memos.teaser: Walking sheets for the 9-to-5er, Soccer Dad, and Grad Student. Four directions, feet that stop when you do.

memos.title: I've never made a game. Here's a green dollar sign chasing a square.
memos.teaser: A photographer, Vampire Survivors, and the moment midlife became a bullet hell.
